cards.text: Abraham and his wife Sarah have been waiting on a son. The LORD told Abraham that Sarah would have one, and Sarah, listening at the tent entrance, laughed to herself (Genesis 18:10-12). Now, friend, the LORD attends to Sarah, and she conceives.

cards.question: The LORD once said Sarah's son would come at a set time (Genesis 18:14). When does Sarah's son arrive?

answers.text: At the very time God had promised
A full year after the promised time
Many years after the promised time

cards.text: Sarah bears Abraham a son in his old age, right on God's schedule. Friend, I set a timer for ten minutes, walk away, and come back to a tray of CHARCOAL.
Abraham gives the name Isaac to the son Sarah bore him. No group chat vote, no list of forty options taped to the fridge.
When Isaac is eight days old, Abraham circumcises him, as God had commanded him.

cards.question: When Abraham was ninety-nine, God said Sarah would bear his son at this time next year (Genesis 17:1, 21). How old is Abraham when Isaac is born?

cards.text: Then Sarah says, "God has made me laugh…" She laughed to herself back at the tent entrance, but I bet THIS laugh comes from a whole different recipe.

cards.question: Sarah says God has made her laugh. Who does she say will laugh with her?
Sarah says anyone could have told Abraham that she would nurse children.
Isaac grows and is weaned, and Abraham holds a great ___ on that day.

cards.text: Now, Hagar is Sarah's Egyptian maidservant, and she bore Abraham a son named Ishmael (Genesis 16:1, 15). But Sarah sees what Hagar's son is doing to her son Isaac.

cards.question: What does Sarah see Hagar's son doing to Isaac?
Sarah tells Abraham to send Hagar and her son away.

cards.text: And Sarah says why: "…for the slave woman’s son will never share in the inheritance with my son Isaac!"
This hits Abraham hard: the matter distresses him greatly, because it concerns his son Ishmael. Friend, this isn't some squabble over who ate the last cookie, this is his BOY.
Then God speaks to Abraham: "Do not be distressed about the boy and your maidservant." Friend, when you're tied up in knots, THAT is the voice you want to hear.

cards.question: God tells Abraham to listen to everything Sarah tells him. What reason does God give?

answers.text: His offspring will be counted through Isaac
His offspring will be counted through Ishmael
Hagar will find a better home in Egypt

cards.question: God tells Abraham that nothing will come of the slave woman's son.

cards.text: Early in the morning, Abraham gets up and puts bread and a skin of water on Hagar's shoulders. Then he sends her away with the boy, and I bet that goodbye sat heavy on him, friend.

cards.question: Hagar leaves and wanders in the Wilderness of ___.
When the water in the skin is gone, Hagar leaves the boy under one of the bushes and sits down about a bowshot away. Why does she say she's sitting that far off?

answers.text: She cannot bear to watch him die
She wants to search for water
She wants to pray by herself

cards.text: As she sits there, Hagar lifts up her voice and weeps. Then, friend, a voice comes down from heaven itself: the angel of God calls to her, "What is wrong, Hagar?" and tells her not to be afraid.

cards.question: The angel tells Hagar that God has heard the voice of the boy.
The angel tells Hagar to get up. What does the angel tell her to do with the boy?

answers.text: Lift him up and take his hand
Let him rest under the bush

cards.question: The angel adds, "…for I will make him into a great nation." Then God opens Hagar's eyes. What does she see?

cards.text: She goes, fills the skin with water and gives the boy a drink. I spent years in the back of a dark junk drawer, friend, so I know a little something about the moment the light shows up.
God is with the boy, and he grows up, settles in the wilderness and becomes a great archer. Me? I can't aim one sprinkle at a cookie without it landing on the floor.

cards.question: While Ishmael is living in the Wilderness of Paran, his mother gets him a wife from the land of ___.

cards.text: And that's where we'll leave it for now, friend. Abraham's story still has PLENTY more batches to go.
